steps: Some characters differ only by a dot or a small hook.
Take one character, find all its copies, and cross them off.
Repeat until every character is crossed off, counting types.
There are 21 types.
qs.trap: Treating a character with a dot as the same as one without.

steps: The gaps vary (2, 4, 2, ...), so look for a property instead.
Every number is a prime.
After 109, the next prime is 113 (110, 111 and 112 are not prime).
And after 113 comes 127: the series lists primes in order.

qs.trap: Looking for a fixed gap. The rule is "the next prime".

steps: Follow each line from one end to the other; crossings do not split it.
Mark each end as you count.
Count ends and divide by 2 as a check.
There are 22 lines.
qs.trap: Counting a line twice where it crosses another.

steps: Each T has an outer colour and a centre colour.
Write each as a pair, for example pink-purple.
Tally the pairs.
12 pairs appear only once.
qs.trap: Ignoring the centre colour.

steps: Compare letter shapes: serifs, the shape of a and g, stroke contrast.
Ignore size.
Group words with matching features.
There are 6 fonts.
qs.trap: Counting size changes as new fonts.

steps: Volume 99 cm³; each block is 2 cm³, so at most 49.
Stand blocks upright (2 cm tall) in the 3 × 3 base: 9 per layer, 5 layers use 10 cm: 45 blocks.
The last 1 cm layer is 3 × 3 × 1: 4 blocks lying flat fit.
45 + 4 = 49, reaching the limit.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 126" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="4" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="18" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Volume 3 × 3 × 11 = 99; each piece is 2</text><rect x="4" y="28" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="42" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">So at most 49 pieces (99 ÷ 2 = 49.5)</text><rect x="4" y="52" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="66" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Stand pieces upright: 5 layers of 9 = 45 (10 cm)</text><rect x="4" y="76" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="90" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">The last 1 cm layer takes 4 lying flat</text><rect x="4" y="100" width="228" height="20" rx="3" fill="#FFE3CF" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="114" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.2" font-weight="700" fill="#FF6B0A" text-anchor="start">Total 45 + 4 = 49</text></svg>
qs.trap: Stopping at 45. The last thin layer still holds 4 blocks.

steps: The torus is 7 tall, more than the cylinder's 6, so it bulges above and below.
It is 16 wide, less than 17, so the cylinder side stays.
Top: an outer ring of the cylinder, the torus bulge, and a small disc inside the torus hole. Same at the bottom.
Side + 3 top + 3 bottom = 7 surfaces.
qs.trap: Forgetting the small cylinder discs inside the torus hole.

steps: A row of triangles alternating up and down fits along a side: each extra triangle needs 1.5 cm.
Each row is 2.6 cm tall (the triangle's height), so two rows fit in 6.8 cm.
Each row holds 3 or 4 triangles in 6.8 cm.
The best arrangement fits 8.
qs.trap: Dividing areas (about 11). Triangles waste space at the edges.

steps: Use the symmetry: count one quarter, then multiply.
Count small triangles, then those made of two, three or more parts.
Add triangles that cross the centre lines.
The total is 40.
qs.trap: Missing large triangles that span the middle.

steps: Count column by column: each column is a stack of triangular prisms.
Use the visible top faces to find column heights.
Remember hidden pieces underneath.
The total is 46.
qs.trap: Counting only visible pieces.

steps: Follow the rope from the load, pulley by pulley.
At each pulley, note which side the rope passes: that sets the direction.
Mark each pulley clockwise or anticlockwise.
Count those matching the smallest pulley: 11.
qs.trap: Assuming pulleys alternate direction. The rope side decides.

steps: The minute hand at 50 minutes points to 300°.
Angle = 65° (the key also accepts 1.12 to 1.14 radians).

qs.trap: Putting the hour hand exactly on 7. It moves 0.5° each minute.

steps: Rearrange each word's letters.
flow › wolf, loin › lion, balm › lamb, bare › bear.
god › dog, act › cat, tab › bat, tar › rat.
glow, sit, lane, bit and reef make no animal. Total 8.

steps: Privacy grows with the number of rooms you must pass through from the street.
For each room, count the doors from the outside to reach it.
The room with the most doors to pass is the most private.
That is room 25.
qs.trap: Choosing the room farthest away on paper. Count doors, not distance.

steps: Treat each opening (door or window) as a point where someone could see you.
Try routes through the lanes and count openings passed.
Choose the route with the fewest.
The best route passes 3 openings.
qs.trap: Choosing the shortest route. The goal is fewest openings, not distance.

steps: A triangle needs three points joined by drawn lines, not all on one line.
E, J, G are on one line; so are F, J, H.
Count by groups: 8 in the base, 4 sloping faces, 4 through IJ, 2 diagonal planes.
Total 18 (checked by listing all point triples).

steps: From the figure, each rectangle is twice the size of the one inside it.
So white 6 × 4, red 12 × 8, black 24 × 16.
AC is half the black width: 12. CB is its height: 16.

qs.trap: Using the white rectangle's sides for the triangle.

steps: Meet Mukund first: 1 lollipop › 2 toffees › 6 ice creams.
Then Ranjana: 6 ice creams › 12 lollipops › 36 toffees.
The other order gives far fewer (Ranjana first: 3 toffees, then Mukund: 9 ice creams, stuck).
Maximum: 36 toffees.

qs.trap: Stopping at toffees after the first meeting.

steps: Square partitions can be any size and can be tilted.
Two tilted, overlapping squares placed cleverly can divide the box into 9 separate regions.
Straight, upright squares need more.
The key accepts 2 or 4.
qs.trap: Using only straight walls. Squares can be tilted.

steps: Compare in a grid pattern.
Check hanging items, jars, faces, clothes.
Mark each difference on both.
There are 10.
qs.trap: Scanning at random.

steps: Pick a distinctive detail in each option.
Find it in the photo at the same angle and size.
Mirror or changed copies fail.
B, C and D are parts.
qs.trap: Accepting a mirrored part.

steps: Remove spaces and read the letters as one string.
"humankind, I am afraid" contains INDIA.
"stir another" contains IRAN.
Ghana and Peru do not appear.
qs.trap: Reading word by word. Hidden words cross the gaps.

steps: A puts Pradyuman with Daya: fails.
C splits Fredricks and Salunkhe: fails.
B and D keep every rule; Fredricks is on Donga in both, so the Tirudan rule does not apply.
B and D are acceptable.

qs.trap: Forgetting the "if" rule only applies when Fredricks takes Tirudan.

steps: Read left to right: 2 is the child of 3; 1 is 3's wife; 1 is the child of 4; 5 is 4's wife.
The paper treats 3's wife (1) as the mother of 3's child (2), so D is true.
Then 2 is the child of 1, and 1 is the child of 4, so 2 is 4's grandchild (A).
1 is a wife, so female: she is 5's daughter (B). C is false: 5 is a wife, not a grandfather.

qs.trap: Missing D. The official key takes the wife of 3 as the mother of 3's child.

steps: Closest = small, thin-lined and blue.
Farthest = big, thick-lined and red.
Compare the named circles on all three rules.
A and C are true.
qs.trap: Using only size.

steps: Escher's shapes fit together with no gaps: tessellation.
Shapes switch between being figure and background: figure and ground.
Mise en scène is a film term; collage is pasting materials.
A and B.
qs.trap: Choosing only one concept.

steps: A: power is valuable only as a means (instrumental), not in itself. True.
B: our significance in the universe is a theme. True.
C: nihilism and narcissism are criticised, not suggested. False.
D: totalitarian history shows we seek power, not shun it. False.
qs.trap: Mixing up what the author criticises and recommends.

steps: Pick a distinctive feature.
Rotate the figure to each option.
Mirror images fail.
Only D is a rotation.
qs.trap: Accepting a mirror image.

steps: B: some migrants are men (given). Valid.
C: migrants are not strong, so some people are not strong. Valid.
A: female natives are strong, so some women are strong. Valid (as accepted by the key).
D: male natives are also strong, so not all strong people are women. Invalid.
qs.trap: Forgetting that male natives are strong too.

steps: Scribble and doodle both mean drawing or writing carelessly.
Nibble means small bites; feeble means weak.
Only the first two match.
A and B.
qs.trap: Matching by sound (-bble).

steps: Heart: the central part.
Core: the central part.
Nucleus: the central part.
Nub: the central point of a matter. All four.
qs.trap: Rejecting "nub" as unfamiliar.

steps: Lines like "No one really cares" sound cynical.
Remembering home weddings that "would go on for days" is nostalgic.
Nothing suggests happiness or lust.
A and B.
qs.trap: Reading "Not all that bad" as happiness. The tone is ironic.

steps: If doubt grows with knowledge, a knowledgeable person has doubt (C).
More exactly, their doubt grows as they learn (D).
A and B contradict the quote.
The key accepts C, D or just D.
qs.trap: Choosing "no doubt", the opposite of the quote.

qs.key: A, B, C or B, C
steps: B: practice is knowledge in action. True.
C: knowledge without doing is theory. True.
A: theory comes first, since it already exists. Accepted.
D: they are not the same. False.
qs.trap: Choosing D because both are knowledge.

steps: A, B and C are worried or critical about technology.
D calls the computer "a bicycle for our minds": praise.
Only D celebrates it.
D.
qs.trap: Missing the critical tone in A.

steps: A: gravity carries spring water downhill through bamboo. True.
B: pipes can cross roads overhead. True.
C: it suits places with scarce water, not high ground water. False.
D: PVC pipes can replace bamboo. True.
qs.trap: Ticking C. Drip irrigation is for water-scarce places.

steps: Proximity: the shapes are close, so we see them as one group.
Continuity: their edges seem to continue into lines.
Closure: our mind completes the missing star outline.
The key gives proximity, continuity and closure.
qs.trap: Choosing only closure.

steps: Fold each net in your mind.
Check each face lands in the right place.
Cuts must allow the faces to separate correctly.
B and C match.
qs.trap: Mixing up cut and fold lines.

steps: Ajanta paintings are Buddhist murals with graceful, detailed figures and earthy colours.
Compare each image's style.
H, K, M, J and I fit the Ajanta style.
A, C and D.
qs.trap: Confusing Ajanta with other Indian painting styles.

steps: The paintings are folk or tribal styles painted on walls.
They draw on tribal stories: C true.
They are wall murals: D true.
Not all are from Maharashtra, and they do not use geometric grids.
qs.trap: Assuming all tribal art is Warli from Maharashtra.

steps: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere.
Carbon dioxide and methane are major ones.
Hydrogen sulphide and chlorine are not counted as greenhouse gases.
B and D.
qs.trap: Ticking any harmful gas.

steps: Fold each net.
Check faces and edges line up.
Rule out nets with overlapping faces.
A and D match.
qs.trap: Checking face count only.

steps: B: relaxing categories lets parallels be drawn, so strict categories prevent it. True.
C: meaning and value lie in producing and spreading signs and information. True.
A: "says less about their work than..." is not "only". False.
D: the author does interpret conceptual art this way. False.
qs.trap: Reading "less" as "only" in A.

steps: Read each share from the chart.
Doctors and businessmen together are under half: A true, D false.
Engineers are about a third: B true.
Engineers and designers together are about 60%: C true.
qs.trap: Reading the chart's colours wrongly.

qs.key: B, C or A, B, C or B, C, D or A, B, C, D
steps: A magnifying glass is a convex lens.
A microscope uses convex lenses.
Peepholes and car headlights can also involve convex lenses, so the key accepts several answers.
B, C, or A, B, C, or B, C, D, or all four.
qs.trap: Thinking a peephole uses only a convex lens. It usually combines lenses.

steps: Ravi Varma painted many scenes from Indian epics.
This one shows a woman talking with a swan.
That is Damayanti, who sent messages to Nala through a swan.
D.
qs.trap: Guessing Shakuntala, another favourite Ravi Varma subject.

steps: Kerala is the smallest of the four.
Gujarat is next, then Uttar Pradesh.
Rajasthan is India's largest state.
Kerala, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan.
qs.trap: Going by population: UP has the most people, Rajasthan the most land.

steps: Trace the turns on the map with your pencil.
"Second right" means skip the first right turn.
Count carefully at each junction.
He reaches Kandivali.
qs.trap: Counting the junction you start at.

steps: Doors must let almost everyone through without bending.
So design for the tall end of the population: the tallest 5% of men.
Designing for averages would leave many people ducking.
A.
qs.trap: Using the average height.

steps: Match features seen in both views.
Remember a flat map stretches near the top and bottom.
Check positions across the seam.
C is correct.
qs.trap: Ignoring stretching at the poles.

steps: Phulkari: bright flower patterns stitched in silk on cotton.
Look for dense geometric flowers in bright yellow, orange and red.
Other options show other states' crafts.
C.
qs.trap: Confusing Phulkari with Kantha (Bengal).

steps: A pull shot: weight back, bat swings across the body, finishes over the shoulder.
Look at the frames on either side of the gap.
Choose the in-between pose.
D.
qs.trap: Choosing a frame from another shot.

steps: Diamond + diamond = diamond, and diamond + triangle = triangle: the diamond acts like 0, the triangle like 1.
Triangle + triangle = triangle-diamond, which is "10". So the symbols count in binary (base 2).
Check: triangle + triangle-triangle (1 + 3) = triangle-diamond-diamond (100 = 4). It works.
Triangle-diamond + triangle-diamond = 2 + 2 = 4 = triangle-diamond-diamond: D.
qs.trap: Trying to add shapes like pictures. Treat the symbols as digits.

steps: The flower is frangipani (champa or plumeria): five waxy white petals with a yellow centre.
Frangipani leaves are long, narrow ovals with a pointed tip and many fine side veins running out from a strong midrib.
A is a maple leaf, B is a three-part (compound) leaf and C is a broad oval leaf.
Only D has the long frangipani shape: D.
qs.trap: Choosing C because it is also oval. Look at the length and the veins.

steps: Study the word first: the strokes are the same thickness everywhere and the loops are round and open.
Compare each option letter against this: stroke weight, loop shape and how the strokes end.
A, B and C each differ in weight or loop shape from the word.
D matches the word's construction: D.
qs.trap: Judging only by how bold the letter looks. Compare the loops and stroke endings too.

steps: Each figure is made of five small triangles holding numbers.
The four options repeat the four shapes already in the series, so the shape alone does not decide the answer.
Compare the numbers of each option with the figures in the series.
The official key gives B.
qs.trap: Spending too long: if no rule appears in a minute, mark it and move on.

steps: Two flips at right angles = a 180° turn.
So the result is a 90° turn plus a 180° turn = 270° clockwise (90° anticlockwise).
Turn the figure 90° anticlockwise.
B.
qs.trap: Doing each step separately and losing track.

steps: Jim Corbett: Uttarakhand.
Ranthambore: Rajasthan.
Kaziranga: Assam.
Kanha: Madhya Pradesh.
qs.trap: Swapping Kanha and Ranthambore.

steps: Fold the net in your mind.
Track which letters meet at a corner.
Check letter orientation.
D.
qs.trap: Ignoring letter orientation.

steps: 1: Kathakali, Kerala.
2: Kuchipudi, Andhra Pradesh.
3: Mohiniyattam, Kerala.
4: Sattriya, Assam.
qs.trap: Confusing Kathakali and Mohiniyattam: both from Kerala.

steps: Unfold in reverse order.
Each unfold mirrors the cuts.
Count the cut copies.
A.
qs.trap: Unfolding in the wrong order.

steps: Each mirror flips the triangle across that edge.
Track the triangle through each step.
Count the flips: odd means mirrored, even means rotated.
A.
qs.trap: Rotating instead of mirroring.

steps: A tangram has 7 pieces: 2 large, 1 medium, 2 small triangles, a square and a parallelogram.
The parallelogram cannot be flipped, so check its direction.
Fit the pieces into each option.
A works.
qs.trap: Flipping the parallelogram.

steps: The poem pictures painters as fishermen in oceans of colour.
Both painters and fishermen could drip with paint or water.
The key accepts A or B.
Painters or fishermen.
qs.trap: Taking the poem literally.

steps: "Crawl" can mean moving slowly across a surface.
Text crawls across a screen (a news ticker).
The others do not crawl.
Words.
qs.trap: Thinking only of animals.

steps: Lad Bazaar is a market in Hyderabad.
"Goods ready" and "theatre of give and take" describe selling.
Ali sits in his prime spot sipping tea.
He is a shopkeeper.
qs.trap: Missing the market clues.

steps: The lines describe burps and other noises from inside the body.
"Dignified insides" is a playful name for the stomach.
Occupation and exile describe food going in and out.
Stomach.
qs.trap: Reading it as a country.

steps: After t real hours, the strange hour hand has moved t/2 hours; the minute hand 6t hours.
Match both hand positions in the figure.
Solve for t.
t gives 8:05.
qs.trap: Using normal clock speeds.

steps: Scan in a fixed order: row by row.
Tick each face with a moustache.
Check faces partly hidden.
qs.trap: Counting beards as moustaches.

steps: The logo is an apple with a bite on the right and a leaf tilted right.
Check the bite side, leaf angle and stem.
Compare options.
C.
qs.trap: Missing the bite side.

steps: A convex lens bends light to a focus, forming a real image on the sensor.
Concave lenses spread light and cannot form a real image alone.
Camera lenses act overall as convex lenses.
A.
qs.trap: Choosing both: overall, the lens behaves as convex.

steps: Look at its shape: a cone or basket with an opening.
Such traps are pushed into shallow water to catch fish.
It is not a sieve or winnowing basket.
B: catching fish.
qs.trap: Mistaking it for a winnowing basket.

steps: Match each avatar image to its symbol or story.
For example, Matsya with the fish, Vamana with the umbrella.
Check all five.
C.
qs.trap: Matching only one pair.

steps: Pointillism: dots of colour. Op Art: optical patterns.
Pop Art: comic or advertising style. Surrealism: dreamlike scenes.
Expressionism: distorted emotion. Realism: everyday life, true to life.
C matches all six.
qs.trap: Mixing up Op Art and Pop Art.

steps: Early Picasso: realistic. Then the Blue Period, then Cubism, then simplified late styles.
Place each portrait by style.
Order them.
C.
qs.trap: Ordering by colour alone.

steps: Woodblock prints with bold outlines and waves are Japanese ukiyo-e.
The style is distinct from Chinese ink painting.
This is a famous Japanese print.
Japan.
qs.trap: Guessing China.

steps: After 4 m each, they are 8 m apart.
Turning left sends them in opposite sideways directions: 3 + 3 = 6 m apart that way.
Distance = root(8² + 6²) = 10 m.
C.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 112" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><circle cx="118" cy="60" r="3" fill="#0A2560" stroke="none" stroke-width="1.4"/><line x1="118" y1="60" x2="78" y2="60" stroke="#FF6B0A" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M78.0 60.0 L83.4 57.4 L83.4 62.6 Z" fill="#FF6B0A"/><line x1="78" y1="60" x2="78" y2="36" stroke="#FF6B0A" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M78.0 36.0 L80.6 41.4 L75.4 41.4 Z" fill="#FF6B0A"/><line x1="118" y1="60" x2="158" y2="60" stroke="#FF6B0A" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M158.0 60.0 L152.6 62.6 L152.6 57.4 Z" fill="#FF6B0A"/><line x1="158" y1="60" x2="158" y2="84" stroke="#FF6B0A" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" /><path d="M158.0 84.0 L155.4 78.6 L160.6 78.6 Z" fill="#FF6B0A"/><line x1="78" y1="36" x2="158" y2="84" stroke="#C23A3A" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" /><text x="96" y="56" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="140" y="56" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="72" y="50" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="164" y="74" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8" font-weight="700" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="118" y="104" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="8.6" font-weight="700" fill="#FF6B0A" text-anchor="middle">Across 8, apart 6: root(64 + 36) = 10 m</text></svg>
qs.trap: Assuming both turn the same way. Facing opposite directions, "left" points opposite ways.

steps: In each row, the third figure is the first two drawn overlapping side by side.
Row 1: two hexagons overlap. Row 2: two squares overlap.
Row 3: an upward and a downward triangle must overlap.
Both C and D show this, so the key accepts C or D.
qs.trap: Looking for a rotation. The rule is overlap.

steps: Follow one symbol at a time across each row.
The triangle jumps to the next corner clockwise. The circle moves one cell clockwise round the edge. The star moves one step diagonally.
Row 3: triangle top-left, top-right, then bottom-right. Star bottom-left, centre, then top-right. Circle ends at bottom-right, under the triangle.
So the grid shows a star top-right and a triangle bottom-right: C.
qs.trap: Missing that two symbols can share a cell: the circle hides under the triangle, as in row 1.

steps: Usability: how easily people can understand and use a product.
Functionality: what it does. Durability: how long it lasts.
Aesthetics: how it looks.
B.
qs.trap: Choosing functionality.

steps: Standard sizes let parts from different makers fit together.
Bulbs, plugs and screws are examples.
Stylization and diversification do the opposite.
A.
qs.trap: Choosing "all of the above".

steps: The cut passes through both solids.
The cylinder part gives a curved edge; the cuboid part gives straight edges.
Put them together in their real proportions.
A.
qs.trap: Forgetting the cuboid part.

steps: From matrix 1 to 2, the eight outer numbers all move one place anticlockwise round the edge.
Then the centre number swaps with the bottom-right number.
Check 2 to 3: the same two moves give 3 9 5 / 6 1 2 / 7 4 8. It works.
Apply both moves to matrix 3: 9 5 2 / 3 4 8 / 6 7 1. That is B.
qs.trap: Forgetting the centre swap. Without it you get 1 in the centre and 4 in the corner.

steps: It measures greenhouse gas emissions from an activity.
Often given as the amount of carbon dioxide (or its equivalent).
The key accepts A or B.
A or B.
qs.trap: Choosing the fossil or plant options.

steps: Look straight down on the solid.
Note each part's outline and position.
Compare.
A.
qs.trap: Mixing up front and back.
